customer_question: Our PTS test results show 9 FAIL/Indecisive items for BAS, DIS, and HIDS, even though HOGP passed. What is the likely cause?
question_variants: BAS/DIS/HIDS PTS test FAIL - what features need to be implemented?
Why does BAS Battery Level GGIT table fail in PTS?
Why does DIS PnP ID test fail in PTS for our Bluetooth keyboard?
actual_issue: During PTS profile testing for a Bluetooth keyboard ([COMPANY] Topre), HOGP passed all test items but BAS, DIS, and HIDS had 9 combined FAIL/Indecisive results. Analysis of the PTS logs revealed that the product was missing specific GATT characteristic implementations required by BAS, DIS, and HIDS: specifically, the 'Battery Level' GGIT table (BAS), 'PnP ID' characteristic (DIS), and other mandatory GATT characteristics. The consultant diagnosed: the SW development team likely implemented the same profile set as the previous 2021 keyboard (which did not require BAS/DIS/HIDS), without adding the new mandatory features required by the post-July 2024 registration rules. The product needed firmware updates to implement the missing BAS/DIS/HIDS GATT characteristics before retesting. The Bluetooth failures were entirely independent of the parallel WHQL (Windows Hardware Quality Lab) certification test.
plain_english_explanation: When the Bluetooth SIG updated its registration system in July 2024 to require BAS, DIS, and HIDS testing for HOGP keyboards, it also meant that products must actually implement those services in firmware. A keyboard development team working from their existing 2021 codebase might naturally omit BAS/DIS/HIDS since those weren't needed before. PTS tests for these profiles require specific GATT characteristics to be present and readable: BAS requires a 'Battery Level' characteristic with GGIT (GATT table) format; DIS requires a 'PnP ID' characteristic. If these are not implemented in the product's firmware, PTS returns FAIL (feature not found) or Indecisive (feature found but not responding correctly). The fix requires a firmware update to implement the missing GATT characteristics - this is a product development change, not a test setup issue.
consultant_answer: Since July 1, 2024, HOGP HID Devices are required to support BAS, DIS, HIDS. Testing with the minimum required ICS items for BAS, DIS, HIDS showed HOGP passed all items, but 9 combined items for BAS, DIS, HIDS did not Pass (Fail or Indecisive). The PTS logs indicate that required features - e.g., 'BAS Battery Level' GGIT table, DIS 'PnP ID' - are not implemented. These are test items that became subject to HOGP testing after July 1, 2024. I suspect the SW development team implemented the same profile features as the previous model.
decision_logic: When BAS/DIS/HIDS PTS items fail for an HOGP keyboard product: (1) Check PTS logs for specific missing GATT characteristics (Battery Level, PnP ID, etc.); (2) If logs show the characteristic is 'not implemented' (rather than a connection/timing issue), this is a firmware gap - the product's SW team needs to implement the missing features; (3) Send the PTS reports to the customer's SW development team for remediation; (4) Confirm the Bluetooth failures are independent of other concurrent certifications (e.g., WHQL) so the teams can work in parallel.
final_recommendation: When a customer's SW team is developing a Bluetooth HID keyboard, proactively inform them early in the project that the post-July 2024 HOGP registration requires BAS (Battery Level), DIS (PnP ID and other fields), and HIDS to be fully implemented in firmware - not just HOGP. Sharing the mandatory ICS items and PTS test scope at the start of development can prevent last-minute firmware surprises. Confirm at the start of testing that all required GATT characteristics are implemented before beginning PTS testing.
risk_if_done_wrong: Discovering firmware gaps during PTS testing (rather than during development) delays the certification timeline, as the SW team needs to add implementation, rebuild firmware, and retest. For a product with an 8-month certification deadline, late-stage firmware changes are disruptive.
